name: World Heavyweight Championship
epitaph: GCW's World Heavyweight Championship was first won by Octavian on 22 April 2001. The fed's own record carries 34 reigns on it, across 22 different champions. The longest of known length is Andy Murray's, 269 days from 21 June 2009. Three of its reigns ended outside a match (two vacated, one ended when the holder departed). Johnny Borealis held it at the end of the surviving record.

name: United States Championship
epitaph: GCW's United States Championship was first won by Thirteen on 22 April 2001. The fed's own record carries 39 reigns on it, across 33 different champions. The longest of known length is Karina Wolfenden's, 314 days from 20 November 2010. Two of its reigns ended outside a match (vacated, forfeited). Aimz held it at the end of the surviving record.

name: HDTV Championship
epitaph: GCW's HDTV Championship was first won by Capo on 20 May 2001. The fed's own record carries 48 reigns on it, across 42 different champions. The longest of known length is Jay Terror's, 157 days from 10 May 2007. Sexton Hardon held it at the end of the surviving record, as the Unified Television and Hardcore Champion after the Hardcore Championship was unified into it on 10 January 2012.

name: Tag Team Championship
epitaph: GCW's Tag Team Championship was first won by Wallstreet Hustlers on 3 April 2001. The fed's own record carries 29 reigns on it, across 28 different champions. The longest is Blood Games's, 1113 days from 21 March 2002. Four of its reigns ended outside a match (two vacated, one departed, one retired). Bryan Mayhem held it at the end of the surviving record.

events.note: The federation's own card, Devil's Night 2005 (30 Oct 2005), in the words of the champion Joshua Curtis: "It has been explained to me that the Tag Team Division here in GCW has flat lined and there is no way to revive it and that effective immediately the tag division has died with myself and Ami being the last champions of record." WorldWide 31 (6 Nov 2005) confirms it ("when the tag division got shut down"). The belt was later revived: the federation's own Tag Team Title History gives its reign No. 16 (21 Mar 2006) as won from 'Vacant'.

name: Vanguard Championship
epitaph: GCW's Vanguard Championship's first recorded champion is 'The Silent Assassin' Peter Vetra. The fed's own record carries 3 reigns on it, across 3 different champions. GCW unified it with the Television Championship at Warpath 2007, on 3 June 2007, when Jay Terror beat Katie O'Clare, and Shaman reinstated it in 2011. The federation unified it into the Hardcore Championship on 11 October 2011.

events.title: gcw-gcwonline-2001-hdtv
events.note: At Warpath 2007 the federation staged the Television and Vanguard Championship unification match, "contested under Vanguard Rules... which means the winner of this match can be declared only by 5 second knock-out or submission": Jay Terror beat Vanguard Champion Katie O'Clare, and the timekeeper tossed both belts into the ring for him. Source: the fed's own card, Warpath 2007 (3 Jun 2007).

At Rampage on 11 Oct 2011 the federation staged a one-title-leaves match between Vanguard Champion Shaman — "the last remnant of the Hardcore division, save for the current Hardcore Champion" who "brought back The Vanguard title" — and the Hardcore Champion, Brad Cruz, who won it on the Cruzifix Slam: "Andrews: Here is your winner...the GCW Hardcore Champion...The SoCal Prophet...BRAAAAAAD! CRUUUUUUUUUUUUZZZZZZZ!!!" and "Bryan: What a war that was, and we've got a SOLIDIFIED Hardcore Champion!" The Vanguard title is named nowhere after this night; the card of 10 Jan 2012 still calls the belt 'HARDCORE/VANGUARD' in its billing and its commentary corrects that on air to the Hardcore title. Source: the fed's own card, Rampage of 11 Oct 2011.
events.title: gcw-gcwonline-2001-hardcore

name: Hardcore Championship
epitaph: GCW's Hardcore Championship was first won by Toad on 21 March 2001. The fed's own record carries 41 reigns on it, across 26 different champions. The longest is Trey Tremendous's, 1693 days from about 28 July 2005, a span that takes in the belt's retirement and reinstatement. Twice in 2005 the belt left him and came back the same night, at Warpath and at Dangerous Games. One of its reigns ended outside a match (vacated). GCW unified it into the Television Championship on 10 January 2012, at WorldWide, in a three-way match won by Sexton Hardon. A card of March 2007 calls the belt retired, and a news column of March 2010 speaks of the 'REINSTATED' Hardcore Title.

events.note: The federation unified the Hardcore Championship into the Television Championship in a three-way match between the two champions and a challenger. Its own voice, before the bell: "Bryan: As per the higher ups, the Television and Hardcore title are being unified and, albeit for a short time, one person will leave here as the first double champion since Triumph Frost." And after: "Andrews: Your winner...and the NEW GCW Unified Television and Hardcore champion.....SEXXXXXXXXX-TONNNNNNN......HARRRRRRRRRRRDDDDDD-ONNNNNNNNNNNNN!!!!!" / "Bryan: Hardon pulled through to become the first ever Unified Hardcore and Television champ in GCW history". The direction is the Television title's: the fed's own title log files this match and the belt's next and last match (Dangerous Games of 17 Mar 2012, 'Television Championship Match') under the Television title, and the fed's own title list carries the champion of record. The federation's own name for the belt from this night is the Unified Television and Hardcore Championship; Yale spends the entrance segment failing to coin a shorter one and Bryan settles it — "Let's just stick with the Unified Television and Hardcore title for now". Source: the fed's own card, WorldWide of 10 Jan 2012 (billed 'TELEVISION & HARDCORE/VANGUARD CHAMPIONSHIP UNIFICATION MATCH').
events.title: gcw-gcwonline-2001-hdtv

events.note: The federation's own words, in the closing line of the Vanguard Championship's first title defence: "Vetra has the retired Cruiserweight and Hardcore titles on his form like a gold vest while he holds his Vanguard Title up in the air." The last Hardcore reign the page carries begins 19 May 2005, so the retirement falls between that date and this card. The reversal has the federation's own word too: a news column of 17 Mar 2010 ('The WorldWide Web #1') says "We knew after GCW Radio that the Tag Team Titles had been suspended, which drew the ire of Bryan Mayhem. But Mayhem was satisfied; he gets credit for a Tag Title reign, and now he's the sole holder of the REINSTATED GCW Hardcore Title." Source: the fed's own card, WorldWide of 9 Mar 2007, and the fed's own news post of 17 Mar 2010.

name: Cruiserweight Championship
epitaph: GCW's Cruiserweight Championship was first won by Chameleon on 22 April 2001. The fed's own record carries 11 reigns on it, across 10 different champions. One of its reigns ended outside a match (retired with the belt). Tessa Windsor held it when the record ends; a card of March 2007 calls the belt retired.

events.note: The federation's own words, in the closing line of the Vanguard Championship's first title defence: "Vetra has the retired Cruiserweight and Hardcore titles on his form like a gold vest while he holds his Vanguard Title up in the air." The Cruiserweight Championship's last reign in the record begins 9 Jul 2006 (Tessa Windsor) and the belt appears in no later title match, so the retirement falls between that night and 9 Mar 2007. Corroborated by the federation's own Record Book, whose 'Defunct Titles' section carries exactly three headings — GCW Cruiserweight Title Records, GCW Vanguard Title Records, GCW Women's Title Records — while the Hardcore title keeps its records among the live belts. Source: the fed's own card, WorldWide of 9 Mar 2007.

name: Women's Championship
epitaph: GCW's Women's Championship's first recorded champion is Icebabe. The fed's own record carries 6 reigns on it, across 5 different champions. One of its reigns ended outside a match (stripped from the holder). The federation's own Record Book lists it among the defunct titles.

events.note: The federation's own Record Book carries a 'GCW Women's Title Records' heading under 'Defunct Titles', so the federation itself records the belt as defunct. The heading is empty of records, which is its own honest fact about how little of this belt the federation kept. Source: the fed's own Record Book.
